tasks.title: Events of audit.log
tasks.statement: text is a fragment of /var/log/audit/audit.log. A record looks like this: type=TYPE msg=audit(SECONDS.MILLIS:SERIAL): fields. Records with the same SECONDS.MILLIS:SERIAL form one event (they need not be adjacent). Write a function parse_audit(text): return a list of dictionaries, one per event, in the order of first appearance. Keys: id (the string 'SECONDS.MILLIS:SERIAL'), time (seconds, int), types (list of record types in order of appearance, repeats kept), key, comm, exe (taken from the SYSCALL record, otherwise None), auid (the number from SYSCALL; None if the field is missing or equals 4294967295), success (the string 'yes' or 'no' from SYSCALL, otherwise None), paths (the name values of the PATH records in order, skipping the value (null)), cmd (the decoded proctitle or None). Take values in quotes without the quotes. An unquoted value in the fields comm, exe, key, name and proctitle is a hex encoding of UTF-8 bytes: decode it; for proctitle null bytes separate the arguments, replace them with spaces. The value (null) means None. Find fields as: a name, an equals sign, then a value in quotes (spaces may be inside) or up to the next space. Before parsing, remove a leading 'node=NAME ' prefix if present. Skip lines that do not look like audit records, and empty lines. A space may stand before the colon: 'audit(...) : proctitle=...' is a record too.
tasks.hint: re.match for the record header, re.findall(r'(\w+)=("[^"]*"|\S*)', body) for the fields; keep events in a dictionary plus an order list. bytes.fromhex and split(b'\x00').

tasks.title: A classifier of SELinux denials
tasks.statement: text is a fragment of audit.log. Records of the types AVC and USER_AVC with the text 'avc:  denied  { permissions }' are denials (skip granted and records of other types). Write a function classify_avc(text, booleans, port_types). booleans is a list [name, subject_type, object_type, class, permission]; port_types is a dictionary subject_type -> port type. For a denial take: perms - the sorted list of words in the braces; comm (in quotes, without them; without quotes it is a hex encoding of UTF-8, decode it); stype and ttype - the third part of scontext and tcontext (the type); tclass; permissive - True if permissive=1. Choose the cause and the fix by the first rule that applies: 1) booleans has a row with the same stype, ttype and tclass whose permission is among the denied ones - cause 'boolean', fix 'setsebool:NAME'. 2) tclass is tcp_socket or udp_socket, the perms contain name_bind or name_connect, and stype is in port_types - cause 'port', fix 'semanage-port:PORT_TYPE:PORT', where PORT is the field src for name_bind and the field dest for name_connect (if both permissions are present use name_bind), as a string like in the record. 3) tclass is one of file, dir, lnk_file, sock_file, fifo_file, chr_file, blk_file and ttype is one of default_t, unlabeled_t, user_home_t, tmp_t, var_t, mnt_t - cause 'label', fix 'restorecon'. 4) otherwise cause 'policy', fix 'module'. Merge identical denials (the same comm, stype, ttype, tclass, perms, permissive, cause and fix), increasing count; keep the order of first appearance. A result element is {'comm','stype','ttype','tclass','perms','permissive','cause','fix','count'}. Read a field of a record as name=value (in quotes or up to the next space); a USER_AVC keeps all its text in msg='...': drop the apostrophes at the edges of values.
tasks.hint: re.search(r'avc:\s+denied\s+\{([^}]*)\}') gives the permissions; scontext.split(':')[2] is the type. The grouping key is a tuple of all output fields except count.

tasks.title: AppArmor denials from the log
tasks.statement: text holds kernel log lines (dmesg, journalctl -k or audit.log); some of them are AppArmor messages like apparmor="DENIED" operation="open" profile="..." name="..." ... requested_mask="r" denied_mask="r". Write a function apparmor_report(text): consider only lines that contain apparmor="DENIED", apparmor="ALLOWED" (complain mode) or apparmor="AUDIT"; skip the others (including apparmor="STATUS"). Read fields as name=value (a value in quotes - without the quotes, spaces may be inside - or up to the next space). The target of a line is the value of name; if it is missing, the value of capname; if that is missing too but family is present, then 'family/sock_type' (sock_type is empty if missing); otherwise an empty string. Group the lines by (profile, operation, target, status) and return a list [profile, operation, target, status, count, masks]. The masks are the distinct denied_mask values of the group, in alphabetical order, joined by commas without spaces (an empty string if the field denied_mask is absent). Sort the list by count descending, ties by profile, operation, target and status alphabetically.
tasks.hint: re.findall(r'(\w+)=("[^"]*"|\S*)', line); the group key is a tuple of four fields, the value is a counter and a set of mask values.

tasks.title: A host hardening check
tasks.statement: Write a function hardening(sshd_t, sudoers, sysctl): sshd_t is the output of sshd -T (lines 'key value', lowercase keys), sudoers is the text of /etc/sudoers, sysctl holds lines 'key = value' (the output of sysctl -a). Return a list of findings [id, severity, subject], sorted by severity (high, medium, low), then by id and subject. A finding is not repeated. SSH (compare values in lowercase; for each key use its first line; a missing key gives no finding, except in the last check): ssh-root-login high if permitrootlogin is yes; ssh-empty-passwords high if permitemptypasswords is yes; ssh-password-auth medium if passwordauthentication is yes; ssh-max-auth-tries low if maxauthtries is greater than 4 (the subject is the value); ssh-x11 low if x11forwarding is yes; ssh-no-allowlist low if there is no allowusers and no allowgroups line (subject '-'). For the other SSH findings the subject is the value 'yes'. sudoers: join lines that end with a backslash using a space; skip comment lines (starting with #, #include too), the lines User_Alias, Runas_Alias, Host_Alias, Cmnd_Alias and lines that do not look like 'who hosts=rule' (spaces may surround the =). A Defaults line with '!authenticate' gives sudo-no-authenticate high (subject 'Defaults'). In a rule 'who hosts=(runas) list' the list is split by commas; an item may begin with the tags NOPASSWD:, PASSWD:, SETENV:, NOSETENV:, NOEXEC:, EXEC:, LOG_INPUT:, LOG_OUTPUT: - the tags NOPASSWD and PASSWD apply to that item and the following ones until changed. The item ALL: if NOPASSWD is in effect for it - sudo-nopasswd-all high (subject - who); otherwise, if who is not in {root, %wheel, %sudo, %admin} - sudo-all medium. If a rule has both kinds of ALL, only sudo-nopasswd-all is reported. An item whose first word (without the directory) is one of bash, sh, zsh, vi, vim, less, more, man, find, awk, python, python3, perl - sudo-shell-escape medium (subject - who). Rules of the user root give no findings. sysctl (use the keys present in the lines; a missing key gives no finding; the value is an integer): kernel.dmesg_restrict must be 1 (sysctl-dmesg-restrict, low); kernel.kptr_restrict at least 1 (sysctl-kptr-restrict, medium); kernel.randomize_va_space equal to 2 (sysctl-aslr, medium); net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter equal to 1 or 2 (sysctl-rp-filter, medium); net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects equal to 0 (sysctl-accept-redirects, medium); fs.protected_hardlinks equal to 1 (sysctl-protected-hardlinks, medium); fs.protected_symlinks equal to 1 (sysctl-protected-symlinks, medium); kernel.yama.ptrace_scope at least 1 (sysctl-ptrace-scope, low); kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled at least 1 (sysctl-unpriv-bpf, medium). The subject of a sysctl finding is the value as a string, as in the text.
tasks.hint: Add the three independent parts to a set of tuples; sort at the end with the key (severity rank, id, subject). Track the sudoers tags in a variable that the list items change in order.

tasks.title: A report on setuid and file capabilities
tasks.statement: find_out is the output of find / -xdev -type f \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) -printf '%m %u %g %p\n': lines 'mode owner group path', the mode is the octal permissions together with the special bits, the path may contain spaces. getcap_out is the output of getcap -r /: a line 'path capabilities' (the new libcap format, for example '/usr/bin/ping cap_net_raw=ep') or 'path = capabilities' (the old format, '/usr/bin/ping = cap_net_raw+ep'); in the new format the path is everything before the last space. Capabilities are one clause 'name,name=flags' or 'name,name+flags', the flags are the letters e, i, p (may be absent); skip lines of any other shape. expected is a list of paths that are allowed to have such rights. Write a function privilege_report(find_out, getcap_out, expected): return a list [path, kind, detail], sorted by path, then by kind. The kinds are: writable (detail - the four octal digits of the mode, for example '4775') - the file has the setuid or setgid bit and write permission for group or others (even if the path is expected); setuid (detail - the owner) and setgid (detail - the group) - the corresponding bit is set on a file that is not in expected; cap-dangerous (detail - the dangerous capabilities in alphabetical order joined by commas) - the capabilities include cap_sys_admin, cap_sys_module, cap_sys_ptrace, cap_setuid, cap_setgid, cap_dac_override, cap_dac_read_search or cap_fowner and at least one flag is set (even if the path is expected); cap-unexpected (detail - all capabilities in alphabetical order joined by commas, then '=' and the flags in the order e, i, p, for example 'cap_net_raw=ep') - the path is not in expected.
tasks.hint: The mode is int(t[0], 8); the bits are 0o4000, 0o2000, 0o022. For getcap: if the line has ' = ' it is the old format, otherwise rsplit(' ', 1).

tasks.title: An auditd rules validator
tasks.statement: text is an auditd rules file (audit.rules): one rule per line; skip empty lines and lines that start with #; words in a line are separated by spaces (no quoting). Lines are numbered from 1. Write a function check_rules(text): return a sorted list [line_number, code] without repeats. A line may give several codes. The grammar and codes: -D takes no arguments (otherwise extra-argument). -b, -r, -f, -e take exactly one numeric argument (none - missing-argument, extra words - extra-argument, not a number or, for -f and -e, greater than 2 - bad-value); a line '-e 2' that is followed by more rules in the file (non-empty non-comment lines) gives immutable-not-last. -w PATH [-p PERMS] [-k KEY] in any order: a path without a leading / - relative-path; PERMS - only the letters r, w, x, a without repeats (otherwise bad-perms); a key longer than 31 UTF-8 bytes - key-too-long; an option without an argument - missing-argument (parsing of the line stops there); any other option - unknown-option; no path - missing-argument. -a (or -A) ACTION,LIST: exactly two words separated by a comma, the action always or never, the list task, exit, user, exclude, filesystem or io_uring, either order - otherwise bad-action (no argument - missing-argument). After it come options in any order: -S LIST - names joined by commas without spaces, each is the word all, a number or a name of lowercase letters, digits and _ (otherwise bad-syscall); -k KEY - at most 31 bytes (otherwise key-too-long); -F FIELD OP VALUE as one word, for example auid>=1000, where the operator is one of !=, <=, >=, &=, =, <, >, & (any other shape - bad-field-syntax); the field is one of arch, auid, uid, euid, gid, egid, success, exit, path, dir, perm, key, pid, exe (otherwise unknown-field); for perm - as PERMS above (bad-perms), arch - only b32 or b64 (bad-arch), path and dir - start with / (relative-path), success - 0 or 1 (bad-value), key - at most 31 bytes (key-too-long). An option without an argument - missing-argument (parsing of the line stops); any other word - unknown-option. Extra checks of an -a rule: if the list is known, is not exit and the line has a field path, dir or perm - field-needs-exit; if there is an -S and no arch field - no-arch. Any other first option of a line - unknown-option.
tasks.hint: Build a dictionary line number -> words for the meaningful lines only. For -a and -w parse the options in a loop with an index i that moves by 2 when an option has an argument; collect the codes in a set.

tasks.title: Exam 1: a virtual machine stopped
tasks.statement: Incident: a virtual machine is not running. The responder collected a dictionary of texts a: 'vm' - the name of the machine; 'virsh_list' - the output of virsh list --all (columns Id, Name, State; a state can have two words, for example 'shut off'); 'dmesg' - the kernel log; 'audit_log' - a fragment of audit.log; 'qemu_log' - the QEMU log of the machine. Any key except 'vm' may be missing (treat it as an empty text). Write a function diagnose_vm(a): return a dictionary {'cause': ..., 'evidence': [...], 'fix': ...}. The decision order is the first rule that applies. 1) In virsh_list the machine vm is in the state 'running' - cause 'healthy', fix 'none'. 2) dmesg has a line 'Out of memory: Killed process PID (NAME)' or 'Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process PID (NAME)' where NAME starts with 'qemu' (kills of other processes do not count). If there are several such lines, the last decides. 'Memory cgroup out of memory' - cause 'oom_cgroup', fix 'raise-memory-limit'; 'Out of memory' - cause 'oom_host', fix 'reduce-overcommit'. 3) audit_log has an avc: denied record whose comm starts with 'qemu' or whose subject type (the third part of scontext) starts with 'svirt' (spaces may stand between avc: and denied). If there are several such records, the last decides. cause 'selinux'. The fix, the first that applies: the object type (the third part of tcontext) is nfs_t - 'set-boolean-virt-use-nfs'; the object type is one of default_t, unlabeled_t, user_home_t, tmp_t, var_t, mnt_t, or scontext and tcontext both have a fifth part (categories like c1,c2) and they differ - 'relabel-image'; otherwise 'review-denial'. 4) dmesg has a line with apparmor="DENIED" and profile="libvirt-..." (the profile name starts with libvirt-) - cause 'apparmor', fix 'fix-profile'. 5) Otherwise cause 'unknown', fix 'collect-more'. The evidence is a sorted list of keys: healthy - ['virsh_list']; oom_host and oom_cgroup - ['dmesg']; selinux - ['audit_log'] and, if qemu_log contains 'Permission denied', also 'qemu_log'; apparmor - ['dmesg'] and, under the same condition, 'qemu_log'; unknown - [].
tasks.hint: Go down the rules and return the result of the first that fires. Read AVC fields with re.findall, the type is split(':')[2], the categories are split(':')[4].

tasks.title: Exam 2: "No space left on device"
tasks.statement: Incident: a write to disk ended with the error 'No space left on device', although there may be free space. The dictionary of texts a: 'journal' - journal lines; 'df' - the output of df -k (columns Filesystem 1K-blocks Used Available Use% Mounted on; the mount point is everything after the 5th column, it may contain spaces); 'df_i' - the output of df -i (Filesystem Inodes IUsed IFree IUse% Mounted on; IUse% may hold '-'); 'lsof_deleted' - the output of lsof +L1 (columns COMMAND PID USER FD TYPE DEVICE SIZE/OFF NLINK NODE NAME; the file name is everything after the 9th column and ends with the word '(deleted)'); 'lvs' - the output of lvs --noheadings --separator ';' -o lv_name,vg_name,lv_attr,data_percent,metadata_percent (fields that do not apply to thin volumes are empty). The keys 'lsof_deleted' and 'lvs' may be missing. Write a function diagnose_enospc(a): return {'cause': ..., 'evidence': [...], 'fix': ...}. The decision order. 0) Find in journal the first line with 'No space left on device' that contains a path: the first substring that starts with '/' and runs up to a space, a quote (' or "), a colon, a comma or a semicolon. If there is no such line - cause 'not_enospc', fix 'look-elsewhere', evidence ['journal']. 1) The filesystem of the path is the df row with the longest mount point that equals the path or is a directory prefix of it on a name boundary ('/' always fits; '/var/lib/images' is not a prefix of '/var/lib/images2/a'). If its Use% is at least 95: add up the sizes (SIZE/OFF) of the deleted files in lsof_deleted whose paths lie on the same filesystem (the same longest mount point); count one file (equal DEVICE and NODE) once; skip lines whose size is not a number. If the sum in bytes is at least 10% of the size of the filesystem (1K-blocks * 1024) - cause 'deleted_open', fix 'restart-holder-process', evidence ['df', 'journal', 'lsof_deleted']; otherwise cause 'disk_full', fix 'free-or-extend', evidence ['df', 'journal']. 2) Otherwise, if IUse% of that mount point in df_i is at least 95 - cause 'inodes_exhausted', fix 'remove-small-files', evidence ['df_i', 'journal']. 3) Otherwise, if lvs has a thin pool (the first letter of lv_attr is 't') whose data_percent or metadata_percent is at least 95 - cause 'thin_pool_full', fix 'extend-thin-pool', evidence ['journal', 'lvs']. 4) Otherwise cause 'unexplained', fix 'check-quota-and-reserved', evidence ['df', 'df_i', 'journal'].
tasks.hint: First the path from the journal, then the longest mount point with a name-boundary check. For lsof: t[5] is DEVICE, t[6] the size, t[8] NODE, t[9:-1] the name.

tasks.title: Exam 3: the host fell off the network
tasks.statement: Incident: after a configuration change the administrator cannot reach the host over SSH. The dictionary of texts a (all values are strings): 'iface' - the name of the management interface; 'client' - the administrator's IPv4 address; 'port' - the SSH port (a number as a string); 'ip_addr' - the output of ip addr (an interface header '2: eth0: <FLAGS> mtu ... master br0 state UP ...', the word master appears only on a bridge port; below it lines '    inet ADDRESS/LENGTH ...'; ignore inet6 lines); 'ip_route' - the output of ip route; 'nft_ruleset' - the output of nft list ruleset; 'ss_listen' - the output of ss -tln. Write a function diagnose_lockout(a): return {'cause': ..., 'evidence': [...], 'fix': ...}. The decision order is the first rule that applies, from the lower layers to the upper ones. 1) The interface iface is not in ip_addr - cause 'iface_missing', fix 'restore-interface-config', evidence ['ip_addr']. 2) The interface (or the bridge it is a port of, if it has a master and the bridge block is in the output) is in state DOWN or has the flag NO-CARRIER - 'link_down', 'bring-link-up', ['ip_addr']. 3) The interface has a master, the interface itself carries an inet address, and the bridge has none (or the bridge block is absent) - 'address_on_port', 'move-address-to-bridge', ['ip_addr']. 4) The holder of the address (the bridge if the interface has a master and the bridge block exists, otherwise the interface itself) has no inet line - 'no_address', 'assign-address', ['ip_addr']. 5) Routes. Connected networks are the ip_route lines that do not start with default, contain the words 'scope link' and do not contain the word linkdown; their first word is the network. If the address client lies in a connected network, the routes are enough. Otherwise: no default line - 'no_default_route', 'add-default-route', ['ip_route']; the first default line has 'via GATEWAY' but the gateway lies in no connected network - 'gateway_unreachable', 'fix-gateway', ['ip_route']. 6) The firewall. Consider base chains with 'hook input' in tables of the families ip and inet; each one decides on its own, and its packet is bad if the verdict is drop or reject. The packet is a new TCP connection from client to port. The rules of a chain go top to bottom; the first that matches decides, and if none matches the policy decides (accept by default). Skip a rule without accept, drop or reject (it does not match). A rule with icmp or udp, and a rule with iif or iifname "lo", does not match. Ignore 'counter ...', 'log ...' and 'comment "..."'. 'ct state LIST' matches if the list has new. 'ip saddr [!=] VALUE' matches if the address client is in (for !=: is not in) the value: an address, a network, a range 'a-b' or a set in braces of those separated by commas. 'tcp dport [!=] VALUE' is the same for port (a number, a range, a set); without a tcp dport condition the port is unrestricted. The verdict of a rule is its word accept, drop or reject. If at least one such chain discards the packet - 'firewall', 'allow-ssh-rule', ['nft_ruleset']. 7) ss_listen has no LISTEN line with the local port port on a non-loopback address (addresses starting with 127. and [::1] do not count; * and [::] count) - 'sshd_not_listening', 'fix-sshd-listen', ['ss_listen']. 8) Otherwise 'unknown', 'collect-more', [].
tasks.hint: Parse ip_addr into a dictionary interface -> {master, state, flags, inet}. For the firewall a line-by-line state machine is enough: table, chain, type...hook, rules; then check the conditions with regular expressions.

tasks.title: Exam 4: the host and its VMs froze
tasks.statement: Incident: the virtual machines on a host hang, I/O is stuck. The dictionary of texts a (any key may be missing - treat it as empty): 'multipath_ll' - the output of multipath -ll; 'dmesg' - the kernel log; 'vmstat' - the output of vmstat 1 N. Write a function diagnose_freeze(a): return {'cause': ..., 'evidence': [...], 'fix': ...}. The decision order is the first rule that applies (errors first, then load). 1) multipath_ll. A map begins with a line like 'name (WWID) dm-N ...' or 'WWID dm-N ...'; the next line 'size=... features=...' shows whether the word queue_if_no_path is in features. A path is a line with the words 'H:C:T:L device major:minor DM_STATE PATH_STATE DEVICE_STATE', for example '5:0:0:1 sdb 8:16 failed faulty offline'. A map is 'down' if it has at least one path and no path has DM_STATE equal to active. If at least one down map has queue_if_no_path - cause 'multipath_hang', fix 'restore-paths-limit-queueing'; otherwise, if any map is down - cause 'multipath_failed', fix 'restore-san-paths'. Evidence in both cases ['multipath_ll']. 2) dmesg, lines 'nfs: server NAME not responding, still trying' and 'nfs: server NAME OK'. For each server only the last such line matters; if for at least one server it is 'not responding' - cause 'nfs_hung', fix 'check-nfs-server-and-network', evidence ['dmesg']. 3) dmesg, lines with 'I/O error, dev DEVICE,'. If some device has at least three such lines - cause 'disk_error', fix 'replace-disk-check-raid', evidence ['dmesg']. 4) vmstat. The header is the line that has the words wa and id (column names: r b swpd free buff cache si so bi bo in cs us sy id wa st, newer versions may add gu at the end); the data lines are lines of numbers with the same number of words as the header. Use the last data line, columns by name. If st is at least 20 - cause 'cpu_steal', fix 'migrate-vms-or-reduce-overcommit', evidence ['vmstat']; otherwise, if wa is at least 30 - cause 'iowait', fix 'run-iostat-find-device', evidence ['vmstat']. 5) Otherwise cause 'no_fault_found', fix 'collect-more', evidence [].
tasks.hint: Split the multipath maps at the lines with 'dm-N'; for paths re.search(r'\d+:\d+:\d+:\d+\s+\S+\s+\d+:\d+\s+(\S+)') is enough. For vmstat use zip(header, values).
